answer: Proof of space defends a jade network by requiring agents to commit non-invertible cryptographic tables to persistent storage. At each verification pulse, nodes must prove ownership of unique disk plots by returning fast lookup proofs. An attacker cannot cheaply spin up synthetic peers; sustaining each pearl node demands dedicated physical sectors, imposing linear disk-space costs per identity. However, datacenters with idle storage can absorb these commitments at low marginal cost.
